style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The fourth of the five closing Hallelujah psalms, and the most physical: a new song in the assembly of the faithful, Israel rejoicing in its Maker and the children of Zion exulting in their King -- with dancing, tambourine, and lyre, Miriam's instruments -- because the LORD takes pleasure in His people and dresses the humble in salvation like a crown. The faithful sing on their beds; the praise does not stop when the assembly disperses. Then the psalm turns martial, and the church has had to read it carefully: high praises in the throat and a two-edged sword in the hand, to carry out vengeance on the nations, bind their kings in chains, and execute the judgment already written -- this is the splendor of all His saints. It is Psalm 2 fulfilled from the other side: the kings who tore off God's bonds are now bound. In the New Covenant the sword with two mouths became the word of God, the nations are conquered by the gospel, and the saints' honor is to reign with Christ -- but the psalm's insistence stands: God's people are not spectators of His justice; they are its agents.

1.text: Praise the LORD! Sing a new song to the LORD, His praise in the assembly of His faithful ones.
1.amp: Praise ye the LORD ['Halleluiah', halelu-Yah, the KJV margin]. Sing [shir] unto the LORD [YHWH] a new [chadash] song [shir], and His praise [tehillah] in the congregation [qahal -- assembly] of saints [chasid -- covenant-faithful ones].
1.notes: The fourth Hallelujah psalm, and the shir chadash (H7892, H2319) of Psalms 96 and 98 -- sung now bi-qehal chasidim (H6951, H2623), in the gathered assembly of the faithful. The 'saints' frame the psalm: verses 1, 5, and 9.

2.text: Let Israel rejoice in its Maker; let the children of Zion exult in their King.
2.amp: Let Israel [Yisrael] rejoice [samach] in Him that made [asah] him: let the children [ben] of Zion [Tsiyyon] be joyful [gil -- exult, spin with joy] in their King [melek].
2.notes: Two titles, two joys: yismach be-osav (H8055, H6213) -- glad in the One who MADE Israel, a nation as a work of God's hands -- and bene Tsiyyon yagilu be-malkam (H1121, H6726, H1523, H4428): exulting in their King. Creator and Sovereign, both reasons for the dance.

3.text: Let them praise His name with dancing; let them make music to Him with tambourine and lyre.
3.amp: Let them praise [halal] His name [shem] in the dance ['with the pipe', machol, the KJV margin]: let them sing praises [zamar] unto Him with the timbrel [toph -- hand-drum] and harp [kinnor -- lyre].
3.notes: machol, toph, kinnor (H4234, H8596, H3658): the circle-dance, the hand-drum, the lyre -- Miriam's instruments at the Red Sea (cf. Exodus 15:20) and David's before the ark. The body is enlisted; Israel's praise was never a seated affair.

4.text: For the LORD takes pleasure in His people; He crowns the humble with salvation.
4.amp: For the LORD [YHWH] takes pleasure [ratsah] in His people [am]: He will beautify [paar -- adorn, glorify] the meek [anav -- the humble] with salvation [yeshuah].
4.notes: The reason for the dance: rotseh YHWH be-ammo (H7521, H5971) -- delight, not tolerance. yephaer anavim bi-yeshuah (H6286, H6035, H3444): He ADORNS the lowly with salvation, as with a garment or a crown -- salvation as the beautification of people nobody else dressed up.

5.text: Let the faithful ones exult in the glory given them; let them ring out with joy upon their beds.
5.amp: Let the saints [chasid] be joyful [alaz -- exult triumphantly] in glory [kabod]: let them sing aloud [ranan] upon their beds [mishkab].
5.notes: yaalezu chasidim be-kabod (H5937, H2623, H3519): the faithful exult in the honor just conferred (v. 4) -- and yerannenu al mishkebotam (H7442, H4904): on their beds. Night-song: the praise of verse 3's public dance continues privately where no one is watching, in the place fear usually sings its own song.

6.text: Let the exalted praises of God fill their throats, with a double-edged sword in their hand,
6.amp: Let the high [romemah -- exalted] praises of God [El] be in their mouth ['throat', garon, the KJV margin], and a twoedged [piphiyyot -- double-mouthed] sword [chereb] in their hand [yad];
6.notes: romemot El bi-geronam (H7319, H410, H1627): exalted praises in the throat -- and chereb piphiyyot (H2719, H6374), literally a sword 'of mouths', two-edged, in the yad (H3027). A psalm the Maccabean fighters took to heart, and an image Hebrews 4:12 shares: the sword with two mouths, and the mouth full of praise.

7.text: to carry out vengeance on the nations and punishments on the peoples;
7.amp: To execute [asah] vengeance [neqamah] upon the heathen [goy], and punishments [tokachat -- corrections, rebukes] upon the people [leom];
7.notes: neqamah (H5360) is God's prerogative delegated -- 'vengeance is Mine' -- executed here by the chasidim on the goyim and leummim (H1471, H3816). tokechot (H8433) are 'reproofs': judgment as correction. In Christ the two-edged sword became the word of God (cf. Ephesians 6:17; Revelation 19:15), and the nations are conquered by the gospel.

8.text: to bind their kings with chains and their nobles with shackles of iron,
8.amp: To bind [asar] their kings [melek] with chains [ziqqim -- fetters], and their nobles [kabad -- their honored ones] with fetters [kebel] of iron [barzel];
8.notes: asar malkhehem be-ziqqim (H631, H4428, H2131) -- and nikhbedehem (H3513), their 'weighty ones', in kable barzel (H3525, H1270). The reversal of Psalm 2: the kings who broke God's bonds are now bound; the meek who were crowned (v. 4) lead the procession.

9.text: to carry out on them the judgment already written. This is the splendor of all His faithful ones. Praise the LORD!
9.amp: To execute [asah] upon them the judgment [mishpat] written [kathab]: this honour [hadar -- splendor, majesty] have all His saints [chasid]. Praise ye the LORD [halelu-Yah].
9.notes: mishpat kathub (H4941, H3789): the judgment WRITTEN -- not improvised zeal but a verdict already on record, executed by agents. hadar hu le-khol chasidav (H1926, H2623): this is the saints' splendor -- to serve the King's written justice, which in the New Covenant is the saints' co-reign with Christ (cf. 1 Corinthians 6:2; Revelation 2:26-27). The Hallelujah closes it, as always.
